2609.20081.title: Reading Emotions in the Token Space: Discriminative Adaptation of SpeechLLMs for Emotion Recognition
2609.20081.paper_summary: SpeechLLMs have shown strong potential for emotion recognition, yet they read the predicted emotion off a generative decoder not suited for classification: it can emit labels outside the target set and favors frequent classes. We propose a discriminative adaptation that reads the final prompt token's hidden state through a classification head, producing a label in one forward pass without modifying the backbone. Because this readout starts from the hidden state the model would otherwise decode, it gives a controlled comparison of generative and discriminative inference in an otherwise identical speechLLM. We keep the head a single linear layer, trading little accuracy for interpretability: each emotion becomes one direction in the LLM output token space, revealing associated tokens. On IEMOCAP, across two speechLLM architectures, it improves Macro F1 and removes hallucinations, with largest gains on realistic ASR transcripts. Our analysis reveals that these emotion directions encode indirect associations mirroring biases in web-scale text.
2609.20081.paper_summary_zh: 語音LLMs在情感識別方面展現了強大的潛力，然而它們是從不適合分類的生成解碼器中讀取預測的情感：這可能會發出目標集之外的標籤，並偏好頻繁的類別。我們提出了一種區別性適應，通過分類頭讀取最終提示標記的隱藏狀態，並在不修改主幹的情況下產生一個標籤，僅需一次前向傳播。由於這種讀取是從模型本來會解碼的隱藏狀態開始的，因此在其他條件相同的語音LLM中，它提供了生成推斷和區別推斷的可控比較。我們將頭保持為單一的線性層，為了解釋性而稍微犧牲準確性：每種情感在LLM輸出標記空間中成為一個方向，揭示相關的標記。在IEMOCAP上，跨越兩種語音LLM架構，它改善了宏觀F1並消除了幻覺，對現實的ASR轉錄有最大的增益。我們的分析顯示，這些情感方向編碼了間接的聯想，反映了網絡規模文本中的偏見。
